item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks A spiking neural network, or SNN, processes information through discrete events called spikes.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a sensor watching a mostly still scene. For long stretches, each part of the scene remains unchanged.

item.title: 1.2 Neurons, Synapses, and Action Potentials
item.description: Neurons, Synapses, and Action Potentials A spiking neural network communicates through the discrete spikes introduced earlier, yet each spike begins with a continuously changing electrical state inside a neuron.

item.title: 1.3 Why Hard Spikes Break Ordinary Gradients
item.description: Why Hard Spikes Break Ordinary Gradients A neuron’s membrane value can accumulate incoming signals over time until it crosses a threshold and emits a binary spike.

item.title: 1.4 Where SNN Efficiency Comes From
item.description: Where SNN Efficiency Comes From Once spikes are understood as discrete events that travel between neurons, the network’s efficiency can be traced through what happens after each event.

item.title: 2.1 The Hodgkin-Huxley Membrane Equation
item.description: The Hodgkin-Huxley Membrane Equation With membrane potential, voltage-gated ion channels, capacitance, and conductance already in place, we can combine them into one quantitative description of a membrane.

item.title: 2.2 Leaky Integration of Synaptic Input
item.description: Leaky Integration of Synaptic Input Membrane potential gives a neuron a short-lived memory of earlier synaptic input, while spike encoding turns each incoming event into a precisely timed contribution to that memory.
